subtitulo: El caminar todos los días es bueno.
regla: An infinitive can work as a noun, matching the English -ing form: (El) caminar es bueno = walking is good. The article el is optional and a bit literary. Infinitives can't go plural, except a few that have become real nouns: los deberes, los placeres, los amaneceres.

bloques.texto: Spanish uses the **infinitive**, not the gerund, as a noun: **fumar es malo**, never ~~fumando es malo~~.
**El** is optional; it gives a slightly more formal or literary feel.
No plural: ~~los caminares~~. Exception: infinitives that became nouns: **el deber / los deberes, el amanecer / los amaneceres, el placer, el poder, el ir y venir**.
Tip: if English says _-ing_ as a subject, Spanish says the infinitive.

lista.es: ==El beber== en exceso puede ser peligroso.
lista.en: Drinking too much can be dangerous.

lista.es: ==Caminar== todos los días es bueno para la circulación.
lista.en: Walking every day is good for circulation.

lista.es: ==El vivir== lejos del trabajo es un problema.
lista.en: Living far from work is a problem.

lista.es: ==El ir y venir== de la gente nos entretenía.
lista.en: The coming and going of people kept us entertained.
I love the sunrises in Mazatlán.

lista.p: In Spanish: _Smoking is bad for your health._
